key_insight: Combining abundant low-fidelity data with sparse high-fidelity simulations via multi-fidelity surrogates (from co-kriging to multi-fidelity neural networks) delivers accurate, cost-effective predictions of composite mechanics across hierarchical scales. The paper shows that hybrid/statistical and neural approaches can trade off accuracy, uncertainty quantification, and computational cost for practical design exploration.
problem_solved: Predictive modeling of composite materials is prohibitively expensive because capturing hierarchical, anisotropic behavior requires many costly high-fidelity experiments or simulations; the paper addresses how to efficiently build accurate surrogates that leverage cheaper, lower-fidelity information.
method: Develop and compare multi-fidelity modeling frameworks ranging from classical co-kriging to modern multi-fidelity neural networks that fuse low- and high-fidelity data.
Exploit hierarchical/scale-aware inputs (constituents → plies → laminates → structures and manufacturing history) so surrogates respect composite-specific dependencies.
Evaluate trade-offs: accuracy, uncertainty quantification, and cost (number of high-fidelity runs) to guide surrogate selection and training strategies.
impact: Provides practical surrogate strategies that substantially reduce the need for expensive high-fidelity simulations, enabling faster design space exploration, uncertainty-aware optimization, and integration of ML models into composite materials workflows.
visual_elements: Fidelity pyramid: stacked icons showing abundant low-fidelity data at the bottom and scarce high-fidelity data at the top, with arrows indicating fusion into a surrogate.
Method comparison chart: bar/column plot comparing accuracy, compute cost, and uncertainty for co-kriging vs multi-fidelity neural networks.
Model schematic: simplified diagram of a multi-fidelity neural network architecture and a co-kriging workflow showing data flow and fusion mechanism.
Application snapshot: annotated composite cross-section or laminate showing hierarchical scales (constituent → ply → laminate) with predicted stress/strain fields.
paper_title: Multi-fidelity surrogates for mechanics of composites: from co-kriging to multi-fidelity neural networks
paper_authors: Haizhou Wen, Elham Kiyani, Gang Li, Srikanth Pilla, George Em Karniadakis
